description: Asavexi is a team of young developers and designers in Nicaragua that dreams and is passionate about creating useful technology. We develop digital products and SaaS solutions with one goal clear: transform the informality of our environment into processes precisely solved by using scalable software.
summary:
¿Por qué es importante? Sugerimos un resumen de entre 50 y 200 palabras.
We are ASAVEXI, and this is ASTRAVEXI: medical intelligence so that distance is never a barrier to caring for life. In deep space, a question to Earth and its answer can take tens of minutes, so crews must act onboard without losing their flight surgeons’ support.

ASTRAVEXI compares each astronaut’s vital signs with their own baseline, the cabin’s environmental conditions and the symptoms of crewmates in the same module, telling whether a problem looks individual, environmental or shared. A traffic-light classification turns this into a clear action, and a local language model explains the alert and guides the assessment, even if the crew medical officer is not a physician.

Earth stays in the loop: the mission’s health history is stored offline and synced periodically, flight surgeons are alerted automatically when a crew member reaches yellow or red, and complex cases travel as a complete case packet. The physician replies with one conditional plan that the system guides step by step.

We built the prototype with synthetic physiological data and real ISS cabin CO₂ data from NASA OSDR, addressing an open NASA gap: medical decision support when Earth cannot answer in time.
details:
ASTRAVEXI covers the full cycle of an in-flight health event: early detection onboard, interpretation in context, and confirmation from Earth.

How it works: Astronauts report symptoms on an interactive 3D body model. Our ML engine compares each reading with the astronaut’s personal baseline and, using cabin data and crewmates’ symptoms, determines whether a problem is individual, environmental or shared. A traffic-light system based on NASA-STD-3001 turns the result into a clear action, and a local language model explains it and guides triage. Health records are stored offline and synced periodically with Earth, and flight surgeons are alerted automatically at yellow or red. For complex cases, the crew sends a complete case packet and receives one conditional plan in return.

Benefits and impact: Crews act immediately without losing Earth’s support. Personal baselines reduce false alarms, and shared environmental risks such as high CO₂ surface early. ASTRAVEXI addresses NASA’s open Medical-701 gap and complements existing systems and physicians rather than replacing them.

Tools: Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn), Ollama running [model] offline, [frontend / 3D library], [database] and [GitHub]. We used synthetic physiological data and real ISS CO₂ data from NASA OSDR.

Creativity: We ask a question most health monitors ignore: is it the astronaut or the ship? We also redesign the medical consultation around delay: one exchange, one executable plan.
